answer: Each agent can claim only one voting weight after locking a scarce deposit that is forfeited if an independent audit proves its identity is duplicated. Audits sample claims at a rate tied to the pulse of new registrations; a detected cluster loses its deposits, while honest agents retain theirs. This makes a sybil campaign costly: the attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it across the whole garden of linked accounts. Spreading claims along a ridge of networks does not remove that exposure.
